Coram : Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ratnaker Bhengra
-------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Rohan Mazumdar, Advocate For the State : Mr. S. K. Tiwari, App
--------
Order No.03/Dated: 19th August, 2023
When the matter is called out, the learned counsels for the parties have appeared.
Petitioner is apprehending his arrest for the offence under sections 414, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120 B of the Indian Penal Code and section 21 of MMDR Act, Rule 7,9 and 13 JMPIMTS Rule.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that allegations are regarding illegal transportation of coal by truck.

He further submits that the petitioner was not present at the spot rather it was the driver who was driving the truck loaded with illegal coal and therefore she does not have any knowledge for the same.
He further submits that she has complied with the earlier order regarding section 41(A) of the Cr.P.C.
He further submits that the petitioner has no criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.
Having heard learned counsels for the parties and in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner, named above.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender before the learned Court below within a period of two weeks from today and on her surrender or arrest, she shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhanbad, in connection with Govindpur P.S. Case No. 450 of 2022, subject to Sudama Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand ... ...
